preconditions.description: The input is a single odd integer x in the range [3, 999999].

postconditions.expression: all(line.strip() in [f'{a} + {b}', f'{a} ^ {b}'] for line in stdout.strip().splitlines()[1:]) and all('+' in line or '^' in line for line in stdout.strip().splitlines()[1:])
postconditions.description: Every operation line after the first is either a valid sum or XOR operation using two numbers already on the blackboard.
The first line is the number of operations q (1 ≤ q ≤ 100000), and the total lines match q + 1.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= int(num) <= 5e18 for num in ' '.join(stdout.strip().splitlines()).split() if num.isdigit())
postconditions.description: All numbers written on the blackboard (including those in operations) are in the range [0, 5e18].
The number 1 appears on the blackboard after all operations are performed.

postconditions.expression: all('+' in line or '^' in line for line in stdout.strip().splitlines()[1:]) and all(' ' in line for line in stdout.strip().splitlines()[1:])
postconditions.description: Each operation line is correctly formatted with a space between the operator and operands.
